Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. Innocent Kaia and Tadiwanashe Marumani will open the innings for Zimbabwe. Curtis Campher will start the proceedings with the ball for Ireland. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Ireland have a competitive total on the board and the onus is now on their bowlers to bowl well and defend this total. On the other hand, Zimbabwe have momentum with them and will be looking to take this momentum into their batting effort. Will their batters step up and chase down this total? We will find out shortly. Back in a bit for the chase...

After Sikandar Raza called it right and opted to bowl first, Zimbabwe were unable to take early inroads with the new ball. They allowed the Irish openers to score freely and at one stage, the hosts looked set to chase a total in excess of 300. However, they clawed their way back into the game by keeping the runs in check during the middle overs. In the last five overs, Zimbabwe did concede 63 runs but they will be pleased with their bowling effort. Tendai Chatara was the pick of the bowlers for them with figures of 3 for 51 from his 10 overs while Brad Evans chipped in with a couple of wickets. Richard Ngarava and Ryan Burl took a wicket each.

A decent end to the innings for Ireland but they will feel that they are at least 15 runs short. Having been sent into bat, Ireland were off to a solid start courtesy of Paul Stirling and Stephen Doheny. The pair stitched a 104-run opening stand to put the visitors in a comfortable position. However, once that partnership was broken, Ireland lost their way and could not keep the scoreboard ticking in the middle overs. Stephen Doheny and Harry Tector did start to get a move on but the departure of the former pegged the visitors back. After the departure of Harry Tector, it was George Dockrell who struck a few lusty blows towards the end to help Ireland cross the 290-run mark.

BYE! The Irish innings ends with an extra! This is banged in short and angling down leg. Mark Adair looks to back away and pull but misses and Andy McBrine is already at the striker's end before the keeper even picks up the ball. Adair also scampers across and no wide is called. Ireland finish with 294/7 on the board!
This is full again and flicked away in front of mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Excellent delivery! Full and angled in at the toes, Mark Adair looks to get the front leg out of the way but misses and the ball goes through his legs to the keeper.
FOUR! Smashed away! This is banged into the deck and angled into the body, Mark Adair walks towards the ball and muscles it in between deep mid-wicket and long on for a boundary.
Back of a length and around off, this is hit away through mid off for just the single.
This is full and straight, Andy McBrine clips it away well in front of the square on the leg side for a brace.
WIDE! An attempted slower bumper, this is around off and loops up over the batter's head. Andy McBrine leaves it alone and a wide is called.
Richard Ngarava will bowl the final over.
This is short and wide, Mark Adair slaps it over the cover-point region and races back for the second.
Mark Adair is the next batter for Ireland.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Tendai Chatara holds onto the catch and picks up his third wicket but Clive Madande seems to be hurt. Another slower short ball around off, George Dockrell looks to pull it away over mid-wicket but gets a top edge. The ball goes high and lands around short leg. Chatara and the keeper both run toward it and keep their eyes on the ball but neother calls for it. In the end, Chatara does take it but Madande bumps hard into him and the physio is out to have a look at the keeper. Hope, he is fine.
SIX! BOOM! Misses the yorker and ends up serving a low full toss on leg stump. George Dockrell clears the front leg and smokes it over the cow corner fence for a biggie.

What happened here? This is on a length and around off, George Dockrell backs away and clobbers it right back at the bowler. The batters look to scamper across but Tendai Chatara is quick to pick up the deflected ball and throws it back onto the stumps at the bowler's end. Andy McBrine is able to get back in and if Chatara kept his presence of mind then Dockrell was struggling to get back to the opposite end.
FOUR! Bangs in a bumper over middle, George Dockrell takes it on and hooks it one-bounce into the mid-wicket fence.
Slower one, bowled into the deck and around off, Andy McBrine pulls it down to long on for a run.
Full again and angling in at the toes, Andy McBrine jams it out to mid on and scampers through for the quick single.
Full and following the batter past the leg stump, George Dockrell looks to clip it away but gets it down to long on for only a single.
Slower and shorter, at the body, Andy McBrine swivel-pulls it down to fine leg and turns the strike over.
Back of a length and outside off, Dockrell stays back and dabs it down to third man for a single.
FOUR! Hammered away! Short and around off, George Dockrell backs away and pulls it right back past the man at mid off for a boundary.
This is banged in short and outside off, George Dockrell steps out and pulls it over wide mid off for a couple of runs.
Fullish length angling across the left-hander, Andy McBrine leaves it alone.
Andy McBrine comes out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another one bites the dust and Tendai Chatara pulling things back nicely here for Zimbabwe. This is full and outside off stump, Curtis Campher stays deep in his crease and looks to loft it over mid off. Campher is unable to get under it and ends up slicing it straight to Gary Ballance at mid off and he makes no mistake, taking his fourth catch of the game. Chatara strikes twice in one over.
Commentary.Howout: c Gary Ballance b Tendai Chatara

Commentary.Commentary: This is shorter and on the stumps, Curtis Campher works it off the back foot past square leg for a couple of runs.
Length ball around off, Curtis Campher shuffles across and looks for the scoop but gets struck on the pads. There is an appeal for lbw but it is turned down.
Short and outside off, cut away but straight to the man at point.
Curtis Campher is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! High, very high but just not long enough. Tendai Chatara goes wide of the crease and bowls the off-cutter into middle and leg stump. Harry Tector picks it up and looks to dispatch it over the square leg fence but isn't able to get much power on it. Tector lofts it really high and Ryan Burl at deep square leg settles under it nicely to take the catch. Tector departs after yet another classy knock.
Commentary.Howout: c Ryan Burl b Tendai Chatara

Commentary.Commentary: Tendai Chatara (8-0-36-0) comes back on.
This full again and around middle, Harry Tector drills it right back at the bowler who does get a hand on it. The ball rolls toward mid off and they get the single.
Raza finds the blockhole this time on middle and leg, Dockrell digs it out through mid-wicket and rotates the strike.
FOUR! This is fuller and quicker but down leg, George Dockrell gets a fine tickle on it and the ball runs away into the fine leg fence.
On a nagging length and around off, George Dockrell looks to cut but is well beaten.
This is full on middle and leg, Harry Tector drives it down to long on for a run.
Dockrell pre-meditates and moves past the leg stump, Sikandar Raza gives it more air and follows the batter as well. Dockrell works it in front of mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Short and at the batter, Harry Tector stands tall and pulls this one to the right of deep square leg for a boundary.
SIX! STRAIGHT HIT! Full and outside off by Brad Evans, right in the slot for the batter, Harry Tector does not miss out and thumps this one down the ground for a maximum.
WIDE! Back of a length but down the leg side, Harry Tector gets inside to scoop this one fine on the leg side but misses. The umpire signals a wide.
Slower and tad short on off, George Dockrell tries to slap this one on the off side but gets an inside edge to fine leg for a single.
Fullish outside off, Harry Tector opens the bat face and slices this one through point. The fielder at deep cover puts in a dive and saves a run for his side.
FOUR! Fuller outside off, Harry Tector gets into the position early and slogs across the line. Gets it towards the vacant deep mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Slower and back of a length on off, Harry Tector looks to pull this one but misses as he gets deceived by the pace of the delivery.
Fuller at the stumps, Harry Tector uses his feet and knocks it down to long on for a single.
Fullish on leg, George Dockrell clips it to mid-wicket for a single.
Short at the stumps, Harry Tector pushes it down to long on for a single.
Loud appeal! Short around off, Harry Tector goes for the reverse paddle but misses. The ball strikes him outside the line and the umpire turns down the appeal from Sikandar Raza.
Full on middle, George Dockrell tries to defend but gets an inside that rolls to square leg for a single.
Fullish delivery at the pads, Harry Tector works this one to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Sikandar Raza (7-0-34-0) brings himself back into the attack.
Another shortish delivery outside off, George Dockrell tries to work it on the off side but misses.
WIDE! Banged in short on middle, George Dockrell tries to slap this one but misses as the ball sails over his head.
Short of a length on leg, Harry Tector pulls this one down to fine leg for a single.

FOUR! FIFTY for Harry Tector! Full and outside off, Harry Tector frees his arms and goes for the drive. Ends up getting an outside edge that goes to the third man fence for a boundary to bring up his fifty.
Another cutter on a length on leg, George Dockrell hangs back and helps this one towards fine leg for a single.
WIDE! On a length but down the leg side, George Dockrell looks to help it fine but misses and the umpire signals a wide.
Slower and short on middle, George Dockrell makes room and slaps this one on the off side. Does not get it from the middle part of the bat but enough to clear mid off and batters run two.
Slower and short on off, Harry Tector waits for it and pulls this one to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Good bumper! Banged in short at the batter, George Dockrell ducks under it and lets it go through to the keeper.
George Dockrell is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Slower and into the wicket on off, Lorcan Tucker makes room to go through the off side but ends up slicing this one high in the air. It goes only as far as backward point where Chamu Chibhabha settles under it and does the rest. That brings an end to the struggles of Lorcan Tucker at the crease.
Commentary.Howout: c Chamu Chibhabha b Richard Ngarava

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length on off, Harry Tector pushes this one to the right of the bowler and takes a quick single.
Short and outside off, Harry Tector punches this one along the ground on the off side. Calls for two immediately and does complete the second run.
Short of a length on off, Harry Tector stays on the back foot and guides this one past backward point. Hits it wide of third man and that allows him to come back for the second.
WIDE! Richard Ngarava bangs this one short but down the leg side, Harry Tector leaves it alone and the umpire signals a wide.
Back of a length at the batter, Lorcan Tucker moves to the leg side and drills this one wide of mid off. Gary Ballance makes a good diving stop to this right and keeps it to one.
Brad Evans follows the batter and bowls a yorker, Lorcan Tucker squeezes this one out to mid-wicket and collects a single.
On a length at the stumps, Lorcan Tucker gets down to slog sweep and helps this one wide of fine leg for a couple of runs.
Tad fuller at the stumps, Harry Tector presents a straight bat and drives it down to long on for a single.
Back of a length outside off, Lorcan Tucker opens the bat face and steers this one down to third man for a single.
On a length outside off, Lorcan Tucker uses his feet and dabs it to backward point for a dot.
Slower and back of a length on off, Harry Tector shuffles across and nudges it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Time for Powerplay 3! Zimbabwe can now have a maximum of 5 fielders outside the 30-yard circle.
Slower one, on a good length and around off, Lorcan Tucker dabs it toward backward point.
Slight halt! Richard Ngarava is experiencing some cramps in his left leg and requires medical attention. He is back on his feet to complete his over.

Tucker just can't find the gaps at the moment. Short again, Tucker comes down the track and flat-bats the pull straight back. Richard Ngarava tries to get down low to his left but fails to get a hand on it and the ball crashes into the stumps at the non-striker's end.
Straight to the man again! This is short and over middle, Lorcan Tucker pulls it toward mid-wicket.
This is short and a bit wide as well, Lorcan Tucker throws his hands at it but hits it straight to the man at point.
Around the top of off, Tucker backs away and opens the face of the blade to ease it toward point.
This is bowled from around the wicket and bowled shorter as well outside off. Harry Tector steers it down to third man for one.
Richard Ngarava (6-0-26-0) is back on.
Fullish length around off, driven to the left of the bowler who makes another decent half stop.
Back of a length and around off, this is dabbed down to the fielder at third man for just another single.

Risky single but they get it with ease in the end. This is pitched up on middle, Lorcan Tucker punches it right back at the bowler who sticks out a right hand and the ball deflects toward mid on. They scamper through for one. The 200 is now up for Ireland.
Good length again and over the stumps, Lorcan Tucker shuffles again and looks for the scoop but is well beaten.

TWO LEG BYES! Good length, angling in from outside off. Lorcan Tucker steps out and shuffles across as he looks to play the pick-up shot. The ball lobs up off the pads and goes toward fine leg. They pick up a couple of leg byes.
Back of a length and angling in from outside off, Harry Tector comes forward and runs it down to third man for a single.
Flighted and on off stump, this is knocked down to long off for a single.
Floated up around off, this is pushed through covers with the turn for one more.
Holds it back a touch and flights it on a nagging length outside off. Tector waits for it and cuts it to the right of the man at point who makes a god stop. They do get the single though.
Floated up around off, Lorcan Tucker reaches forward and pushes it down the ground for a run.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Lorcan Tucker defends it out.

Excellent fielding! This is full and straight, Harry Tector drives it right back and Ryan Burl sticks out his right boot. The ball deflects off the boot toward wide mid on and they get a single. That must have stung Burl as well.
Around the top of off, Lorcan Tucker looks to come forward and drive but gets it off the inner half of the bat through square leg. The batters hurry back for two.
WIDE! Looks to angle this one into the pads but spills it down the leg side. Wide called.
Length again and around off, this is steered through backward point for one more.
Back of a length and over off stump, Harry Tector looks to play it off the back foot but almost gets an inside edge back onto the stumps.
On a good length and around off, Lorcan Tucker looks to punch but mistimes it on the leg side for one.
Chatara sees Harry Tector advancing and bowls it shorter and on the body. Tector manages to work it off the inside edge down to fine leg and picks up a single.
This is pitched up around middle, Harry Tector flicks it straight to short mid-wicket.
Tendai Chatara (6-0-27-0) returns to the attack.
Quicker one, full and well outside off, Lorcan Tucker squeezes it toward short third man.
This is around off, pushed away onto the off side for a single.
TWO WIDES! This is flatter and well outside the off stump, and beats the keeper as well. They cross and a wide is called.
Lorcan Tucker walks out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! Zimbabwe get a crucial breakthrough and the partnership is finally broken. Ryan Burl tosses it up nicely, full and on off stump with the ball turning away. Stephen Doheny has a slog against the turn and ends up slicing it high and over mid off. Gary Ballance from long off comes in and takes a fine low catch. Doheny departs after a brilliant knock and Zimbabwe have an opening here.
Commentary.Howout: c Gary Ballance b Ryan Burl

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter delivery on off stump, pushed through mid off for a single.
Nicely bowled! Holds it back a touch and floats it full outside off with the ball turning away. Harry Tector has a little dab at it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
This is full and wide of the off stump, Stephen Doheny drives it square of the wicket to deep cover for  single.
Fuller one on the pads, flicked away behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
FOUR! A bit of aggression now from Stephen Doheny. This is short again, Doheny comes down the track and muscles it into the cow corner fence.
This is shorter and over middle, Doheny mistimes the pull toward mid-wicket.
Back of a length around off, this is punched away square on the off side for a single.

Ouch, Victor Nyauchi with a moment of madness and Harry Tector isn't pleased at all about it. This is full and straight, Tector drives it back to the bowler who makes the stop and throws it back at Tector who seems to be hurt. Victor says sorry but the umpire calls him and the skipper Sikandar Raza for a quick chat.
FOUR! Driven and driven to perfection. This is pitched up on off stump, Harry Tector plays it on the up and past the diving man at mid off for a boundary.
Victor Nyauchi (4-0-18-0) is back on.
This is fuller and around middle, knocked down to long on for one. Productive overs keep on coming for Ireland as they pick up 8 runs off that one.
Floated up on middle, Harry Tector drives it straight to mid on.
Around middle, this is driven down to wide long on for a single.
At the stumps and punched back firmly toward the bowler.
FOUR! Lovely touch from Stephen Doheny. This is around off, Doheny plays the reverse paddle and gets it fine of the man at short third man for a boundary.
Easy two! This is shorter and on leg stump, Stephen Doheny works it off the back foot wide of the man at deep mid-wicket and picks up a brace.

Time for Drinks! Ireland are going along nicely with Harry Tector and Stephen Doheny out in the middle. With plenty of batting still to come, the visitors look set to post a huge total. These are ominous signs for the hosts and they need a couple of quick wickets to swing the momentum back their way.
Slows it up a touch and flights it on off stump, Harry Tector blocks it out.
Flatter and outside off, slapped away to sweeper cover for one.
This one slides on from the off stump and Harry Tector works it in front of mid-wicket for yet another single.
Looking for two but have to settle for the single. This is a tad short and Stephen Doheny jabs it toward deep square leg for a single.
Loopy delivery around off stump, Tector pushes it down to long off for one more.
On the shorter side and around middle, this is worked off the back foot past square leg for a run.
Half a shout for lbw and nothing more. This is flatter and around off, Stephen Doheny gets an inside edge onto the pads as he looks to flick. The ball rolls onto the off side and they get a single.
This is quicker and around middle, nudged away to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Up and over! This is tossed up outside off, Stephen Doheny backs away and lofts it inside-out over extra cover for a boundary.
Around off stump, pushed out on the off side for one.
This is flatter and at the stumps, Tector blocks it out.
FOUR! Skillful from Harry Tector. This is full and on off stump, Tector goes for the reverse sweep and nails it past the man at short third man for a boundary.
Drops it a bit short and on middle, this is pulled away behind square on the leg side for one.
Floated up on the pads, Harry Tector works it away toward deep mid-wicket and picks up another brace.
This is flatter and around middle, Tector blocks it out.
FOUR! Streaky boundary but Harry Tector will take it. Tossed up full and around off, Tector looks to sweep but gets an inside edge past the stumps and the ball runs away into the fine leg fence.
Tossed up outside off, Harry Tector strokes it away wide of the man at sweeper cover for a couple of runs.
This is pushed through on middle, Stephen Doheny knocks it down to long on for a single.
Ryan Burl (3-0-18-0) is back into the attack.
Touch short on off, Stephen Doheny goes back and punches this one down to long on for a single.
WIDE! Fuller and quicker but down the leg side, Stephen Doheny goes for the flick but misses.
Short and on middle, Sikandar Raza works this one straight to mid-wicket.
Full and at the stumps, Stephen Doheny drives this one down the wicket for a dot.
Raza sees the batter advance and fires a fullish delivery down the leg side, Stephen Doheny somehow manages to get his bat on it as he tried to clip.
Short on off, Stephen Doheny pushes this one back to the bowler.
Tad short at the stumps, Harry Tector works this one towards mid-wicket and takes a single.
Back of a length on off, Stephen Doheny watchfully defends this one out.

Short and on off, Harry Tector hangs back and pulls this one uppishly towards deep square leg. Victor Nyauchi there decides not to go for the catch and Sikandar Raza isn't pleased one bit with his effort. The batters cross for a single.
Back of a length on off, Harry Tector punches this one back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, Harry Tector sways away and leaves it alone.

FOUR! Streaky but Harry Tector will take it! Short and outside off, Harry Tector tries to cut this one hard on the off side but gets an outside edge that flies past the keeper for a boundary. With this boundary, Harry Tector becomes the quickest Irish player to score 1000 runs in ODIs.
Short of a length outside off, Stephen Doheny opens the bat face to guide this one towards third man. Gets a top edge that goes towards third man for a single.
Tad short on off, Harry Tector blocks this one out on the off side.
Tossed up, full on off, Stephen Doheny leans forward and drives it to long on for a single.
Floated, full outside off, Stephen Doheny works this one towards mid-wicket but fails to get it past the fielder.
Short outside off, Harry Tector punches this one down to long on and takes a single.
Fuller around off, Harry Tector defends this one back to the bowler.
Full on off, Harry Tector pushes this one straight to cover.
Another short delivery outside off, Stephen Doheny stays inside and lets the ball go through to the keeper.
Short and at the batter, Harry Tector gets into an awkward position and fends this one towards backward square leg for a single.
Back of a length outside off, Harry Tector dabs it to backward point for a dot.
Short and outside off, Harry Tector sways away and leaves it alone.
Harry Tector is the new man in.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! Brad Evans bowls a short-of-a-length delivery outside off, and Murray Commins hangs back and tries to carve this one on the off side. Ends up getting a thickish outside edge that flies all the way to third man. Gary Ballance there makes no mistake and completes a good catch. Brad Evans delivers the goods for Zimbabwe once again.
Commentary.Howout: c Gary Ballance b Brad Evans

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length at the batter, Stephen Doheny works this one towards mid-wicket and collects a single.
Short and outside off, Murray Commins looks to pull but misses.
Full and outside off, Murray Commins frees his arms and drives this one firmly along the ground to deep cover. Tadiwanashe Marumani in the deep dives to his left and keeps it to two.
Short and turning away on off, Stephen Doheny accounts for the turn and opens the bat face at the last moment. Gets it past short third man and a slight fumble there allows the batters to run three.
Floated, full on off, Murray Commins drives it down to long off and takes a single.
Short on middle, Murray Commins works this one straight to mid-wicket.
Short on off, Stephen Doheny pushes this one to the left of mid-wicket. A fumble there allows the batters to cross for a single.
Full and angling at the pads, Stephen Doheny clips this one to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Shortish delivery on off, Stephen Doheny hangs back and defends this one out.
Slower and into the wicket on middle, Stephen Doheny makes room and slaps this one down the ground for a couple of runs.
NO BALL! Another bumper aimed at the batter, Stephen Doheny once again ducks and leaves it alone. It is called a No Ball for it being the second bouncer of the over.
Banged in short on off, Stephen Doheny shuffles across and ducks under the delivery.
Good-length delivery, angling away outside off, Murray Commins drives away from the body and gets a thickish outside edge. The ball rolls to third man for a single.
Back of a length outside off, Stephen Doheny uses his feet and steers this one down to third man for a single.
Short on off, Murray Commins works this one straight to cover.
Full around off, Murray Commins drives it straight to cover.
Short and on off, Murray Commins defends this one from the back foot.
FIFTY for Stephen Doheny! Short and on middle, Stephen Doheny works this one towards backward square leg and takes a single to bring up his fifty.
Short on middle, Stephen Doheny pushes this one straight to mid-wicket.
A loud shout for LBW but turned down. Googly, short at the stumps, Stephen Doheny goes back to defend this one but gets an inside edge back onto this pads.
A slight halt in the play as Stephen Doheny is feeling a bit uneasy. The physio is out to have a look at him. Doheny seems fine and we are good to continue.
Back of a length on leg, Stephen Doheny gets inside and turns this one to fine leg for a single. He moves to 49 with this single.
Fuller on off, Stephen Doheny shuffles across and clips this one uppishly towards mid-wicket for a dot.
Short of a length on off, Murray Commins opens the bat face and guides this one down to third man for a single.
Beaten! Back of a length in the channel outside off, Murray Commins looks to defend but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Good-length delivery at the batter, Murray Commins block this one out on the off side.
Short of a length and on middle, Stephen Doheny moves to the off side and tucks this one wide of deep mid-wicket and takes a quick single.
Short on off, Stephen Doheny pushes this one to the right of the bowler and takes a single.
Short on middle, Murray Commins flicks this one from the back foot towards deep square leg for a single. Opens his account in ODI cricket with a single.
Short and outside off, Stephen Doheny goes back in his crease and punches it to deep point for a single.
Short and turning into the batter, Stephen Doheny clips it to square leg.
Full around off, Stephen Doheny gets forward and works it to mid-wicket.
Short on middle, Stephen Doheny pushes this one straight to mid-wicket.
The debutant Murray Commins is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Brad Evans bowls a short-of-a-length delivery angling into the batter from over the wicket, Paul Stirling hangs back and tries to help this one towards the fine leg fence. Does not get enough bat on it to clear the man at ropes and holds out to Gary Ballance at fine leg. Zimbabwe have finally broken the opening stand and they will be relieved to see the back of Paul Stirling.
Commentary.Howout: c Gary Ballance b Brad Evans

Commentary.Commentary: Full at the stumps, Paul Stirling pushes this one straight to mid-wicket.
Fuller on off, Stephen Doheny shuffles across and clips it to mid-wicket. A fumble there allows the batters to cross for a single.
Short of a length on off, Stephen Doheny blocks this one out on the off side.
WIDE! Another bumper aimed at the batter but this one sails over the head of the batter and the umpire calls it a wide.
Banged in short on middle, Stephen Doheny ducks under the delivery and lets it go.
Back of a length at the batter, Paul Stirling pulls this one along the ground to fine leg for a single.
Nicely tossed up, full and around off, Paul Stirling pushes it through mid off and picks up a single.
Floated up outside off, Paul Stirling drives it straight to cover.
On off stump, Stephen Doheny pushes it through covers for a run and the 100 is up for Ireland.
Flatter one outside off, this is punched away to sweeper cover for another single.
WIDE! Tries to bowl it full and quick and outside off but spills it beyond the tramline. Left alone for a wide.
Drops it shorter and bowls it outside off, Stephen Doheny goes on the back foot and taps it to deep cover-point for one.
This is nicely flighted around off, Paul Stirling strokes it with the turn through mid off and collects a single.
Length again on the pads, this is worked away 'round the corner for a run.
Pitches it up now around middle, Paul Stirling punches it straight to mid on.
WIDE! On a good length but angled down the leg side, left alone for a wide.
On a length and on the pads, worked away leg side for a run.
Extra bounce! This is shorter and over middle and leg, Stephen Doheny shuffles across and looks to tuck it away but misses. There is a stifled appeal for caught behind but it is turned down.
Fuller but again angling down leg, Stirling flicks it down to fine leg for a single.
SIX! All the way! Brad Evans begins with a short ball down leg, Paul Stirling stands tall and pulls it flat and hard over the backward square leg fence for a maximum.
Brad Evans comes on to bowl, replacing Tendai Chatara.
Tossed up full and outside off, this is driven past the diving fielder at extra cover for a run.
Around off, Stephen Doheny knocks it down to long off for a single.
Excellent running. This is around off and turning away, Stephen Doheny waits on the back foot and eases it behind point for a couple of runs.

Time for Drinks! Having been sent into bat first, Ireland have done well not to lose a wicket against the moving new ball. Moreover, these two kept the scoreboard ticking without taking any risks. On the other hand, Zimbabwe have tried hard but have failed to get any breakthrough.

Tossed up, full and on off stump, Paul Stirling pushes it straight to mid off.
Gives it a bit more air and floats it up on off stump, Paul Stirling defends it off the front foot.
This is flatter again and outside off, Doheny cuts it through point for a single.
Pushes it through quicker and around off stump, Stephen Doheny looks to back away and cut but misses.
Starts off right on the money as Ryan Burl bowls it flatter and on off stump, Stephen Doheny blocks it out.

Good length around off, Paul Stirling keeps it out on the off side.
This is full and straight, Paul Stirling clears the front leg and looks for the big heave but mistimes it badly.
Good length around middle, jagging back in sharply, Paul Stirling looks to tuck but misses and gets hit on the body.

Length ball, angling in from outside off, Stephen Doheny keeps it out.

FOUR! Fuller outside off, Stephen Doheny leans forward and drives this one through extra cover. Hits it to the left of mid off and collects a boundary.
Short of a length on off, Stephen Doheny dabs this one to cover for a dot.

Back of a length on leg, a hint of inward movement, Paul Stirling tries to work it on the leg side but cannot get it away.
Full and angling in on leg, Stephen Doheny clips this one to square leg and takes a single.
Banged in short and aimed at the batter, Stephen Doheny ducks under it and lets it go.

Length delivery at the pads, Paul Stirling clips this one straight to short fine leg for a dot.

Fuller outside off, Stephen Doheny drives this one firmly but straight to mid off.
Back of a length and angling away outside off, Stephen Doheny taps this one on the off side for a dot.

Short of a length outside off, Stephen Doheny pushes this one straight to backward point.
Good-length delivery on off, Stephen Doheny defends this one back to the bowler.

Keeps bowling it back of a length and outside off, Stirling pushes it straight to the man at cover.
Hits the length hard and bowls it outside off, Paul Stirling punches it toward covers.
FOUR! This is shorter and outside off, Paul Stirling obliges the width on offer and cuts it through cover-point for the first boundary of the game.
Bowls it a touch fuller and in line with the stumps, the ball just nips in a bit but Stirling is able to block it out.
Starts off with a length ball that is right on the money. Paul Stirling defends it off the front foot.
Tendai Chatara to bowl from the opposite end.

Done with the pre-game formalities and it is now time to play. The umpires and the Zimbabwe players are out in the middle. It will be Paul Stirling and Stephen Doheny opening the innings for Ireland. Richard Ngarava has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are a few minutes away from the start of the play but first, the two sets of players line up for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Ireland first, followed by the national anthem of Zimbabwe. This is being done in the 2nd game of the series and not the first game as Cricket Zimbabwe have decided to dedicate the proceeds in this game to the family of former cricketer and coach Shepherd Makunura, who along with his wife passed away recently.

PITCH REPORT - Darlington Matambanadzo says that the wicket for this game is the best one so far in the series. Adds that it has been rolled nice and hard and is a bit greener as well. Mentions that the wicket will have more pace in it as well.

Paul Stirling, the stand-in skipper of Ireland, says that they would have bowled first as well. Adds that the wicket can be tricky at the top but it won't be tough for long. Feels that this wicket is different from the last game. Shares that there have been a lot of clutch moments where they have come up on the wrong side. Informs that Murray Commins is making his debut, replacing Andy Balbirnie who is out due to concussion.

Sikandar Raza, the stand-in skipper of Zimbabwe, says that they will have a bowl first. Adds that unfortunately Craig Ervine has got a thing with his finger and it is a precautionary thing to rest him for this game. Mentions that their bowlers did well in the previous game and were a bit unlucky as the edges didn't find the fielders and hopes that they can pick early wickets here. Mentions that the wicket looks good and it could be a high-scoring game. Informs that Chamu Chibhabha comes in to replace Craig Ervine and they have got a couple of additional changes as well.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Stephen Doheny, Murray Commins (On debut) (In for Andy Balbirnie), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Andy McBrine, Mark Adair, Graham Hume, Joshua Little.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Innocent Kaia, Tadiwanashe Marumani (In for Wesley Madhevere), Chamu Chibhabha (In for Craig Ervine), Gary Ballance, Sikandar Raza (C), Ryan Burl, Clive Madande (WK), Brad Evans, Richard Ngarava, Tendai Chatara (In for Wellington Masakadza), Victor Nyauchi.
TOSS - The coin toss lands in the favour of Zimbabwe and they have opted to BOWL first.

On the other hand, centuries from Andy Balbirnie and Harry Tector powered the visitors to a huge total. Their bowlers did put up a fight in the second half but were unable to defend the revised target. Irish fans will be hoping that their side can put in a complete performance and draw level in the series. Will the visitors manage to force a series decider? Or will we see the hosts gain an unassailable 2-0 lead? Let’s find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly...

It’s time for the second ODI of this three-match ODI series between Zimbabwe and Ireland. It has been a fascinating tour so far with T20I series creating a lot of excitement and then the first ODI going right down to the final ball of the game. Zimbabwe though have managed to hold their nerves better and after winning the T20I series, have also taken a lead in the ODI series. Clive Madande was the one who hit a boundary off the last delivery to seal the first ODI for the hosts but the real stars of the show were Ryan Burl and Sikandar Raza who took the bull by the horns and stitched up a counter-attacking stand when Zimbabwe were in a spot of bother with four wickets down early. Zimbabwe will hope that two in-form all-rounders will continue to excel but it is also important for their top order to contribute more if they want to win matches consistently in this format. Their bowlers too looked short of ideas in the middle overs and that is where they need to work on to create more impact as a team. We can expect Tendai Chatara to slot into the XI after missing the first ODI and it would be interesting to see what bowling combination Zimbabwe goes with in this second ODI. Ireland, on the other side, did most things right in the first ODI but just could not close out the game. Andy Balbirnie and Harry Tector batted well after losing two early wickets in testing overcast conditions and went onto score centuries to set up a formidable total. Their seamers were quite efficient too but with rain shortening the game, it turned out to be a game of small margins and unfortunately for the Irish, they ended up on the wrong side. However, we can expect them to make a strong comeback here as they have a quality arsenal at their disposal and they just need to be more clinical in their approach. Can they notch up a win and take the series into a decider? Or will Zimbabwe take an unassailable lead of 2-0? Let’s find out as another entertaining encounter awaits us.
